items.caption:
So you bought cashmere…and now it’s pilling? 🧶 Don’t panic.
Pilling is a normal part of owning cashmere you just need to know how to care for it.
Here’s how to remove cashmere pilling safely and keep your knitwear looking its best.

🔗 you can comment CASHMERE for the list of products used in this video or head to my bio
items.transcript: Cashmere is one of my favorite, favorite fabrics. And if there's a staple that I would suggest anyone had in their wardrobe, I'd tell you a cashmere jumper is exactly that. It should be something that lasts for years and years, and you can wear over and over again. If I was still working on the shop floor and I was selling you a cashmere jumper, there would be a couple of things that I would advise you to buy and also a couple of pieces of advice that I would give you about ownership and upkeep. So first of all, let's talk about pilling. I want to show you the pilling on this jumper. Pilling is completely normal. It's just where the fibers are rubbing together and creating these little balls. You can see this jumper is free of pilling around the neck. That's because my coat is often open, so there's not much friction to be had around my neck. But you can see under my arm, there's lots because I'm constantly moving and all that pilling is happening in those areas where there's lots of movement. So let's talk about how to depill your cashmere. There's two things that I would encourage my customers to purchase. The first is a cashmere comb. This is great for people who are going to commit to that very regular maintenance and it will easily get the smaller pills off and is very gentle on the fabric. The second is much more convenient. It's a fabric shaver and this will help you do larger areas in a quicker amount of time and also catch those larger pills that your fabric comb isn't quite getting off. So what I'm saying is don't panic when your lovely new cashmere starts to bobble. It doesn't mean you've made a bad purchase. It doesn't mean it's low quality and it certainly doesn't mean that you should be returning it. Sometimes there's nothing wrong with what you bought. You just weren't told what ownership looks like. If you've got any questions, let me know.

items.caption:
My very easy banana and chocolate muffins.
These are so easy let me know if you give them a go! 

Link of products at bottom of the caption. 

INGREDIENTS: 

225 G SELF RAISING FLOUR
100 G SOFTENED BUTTER
175 G CASTOR SUGAR
2 MED EGGS
1 TSP BAKING POWDER
2 TBSP MILK
200 G DARK CHOCOLATE
2 BANANAS

Full recipe on thefoldinglady.com

Any questions let me know ✌️
items.transcript: So I've got some mouldy bananas, so I'm going to make what I always make when I've got mouldy bananas. I actually only make these when I've got mouldy bananas, and it is banana and chocolate muffins. They're really a banana bread recipe that I just put in to see what they do in muffin cases, and they're actually delish. So let's unwrap my favourite kitchen tool. So you're going to want to put your mixer attachment on, and then we're going to put all the ingredients in one by one and give it a mix. So we've got flour, caster sugar, two eggs, room temperature butter. Really important that it's room temperature. Teaspoon of baking powder, and two tablespoons of milk, and then your mouldy bananas too. Then we're just going to mix it all together. And when it gets to the point where it looks like it's all mixed, we'll just add our chocolate chips, and then gently give it another stir. You can put in as many chocolate chips as you like, depending on how chocolatey or non-chocolatey you want it. Just make sure you save some to sprinkle on the top before they go in the oven. I actually prefer putting them in the brown paper tulip cases, because I feel like they're big enough for a breakfast muffin, but they didn't have any in the shop, so small ones it is. So I go with the theory of filling any size case a third of the way, and that should be perfect for muffins. And I read that online somewhere, can't remember where, probably Mary Berry, and it's never failed. Oh sorry, not a third of the way, two thirds of the way. Then we're just going to put them in the oven for about 20 minutes. I'm not very good on my oven timings, but I do usually go 180, 20 minutes, keep checking in the last five minutes. Best oven gloves in the world are gut gloves. Nice and brown. I'm pleased with those. There's more to go. But can you see why I like the bigger cases, because it makes so many. But luckily we've got family around tomorrow, so. Okay, we'll have to wait for them to cool down, then we'll crack one open and I'll show you how delicious they are. So I've broken one up, I actually already tried it. So delicious, so delicious. These are my favorite muffins. So good. So good, so easy. Let me know if you make them.
